cards.explanation: The answer is True. Luke says Jesus entered the temple courts and began to drive out those who were selling there (Luke 19:45). The sellers were right there in the courts, friends, and Jesus started driving them out.

The answer is a den of robbers. Jesus says, "It is written: ‘My house will be a house of prayer.’ But you have made it ‘a den of robbers.’…" (Luke 19:46). He starts with what God's house is meant to be, friends. Then He says what the sellers made it instead.

The answer is True. Luke says they could not find a way to do so, "…because all the people hung on His words." (Luke 19:48). The leaders were intent on killing Him (Luke 19:47), but the crowd stuck close to every word Jesus said. So the leaders came up empty, bakers.

The answer is that they ask by what authority He does these things. They said, "Tell us, by what authority are You doing these things, and who gave You this authority?" (Luke 20:2). That's two questions in one breath, friends, a real double batch! They want to know the authority, and they want to know who gave it.

The answer is John's baptism. Jesus asks, "John’s baptism—was it from heaven, or from men?" (Luke 20:4). He answers their question with a question of His own, friends. I'd say that gets everyone's attention in a hurry.

The answer is True. The leaders say, "If we say, ‘From heaven,’ He will ask, ‘Why did you not believe him?’" (Luke 20:5). They can already see the follow-up question coming, bakers. They're checking every answer before they give one.

The answer is prophet. The leaders say that if they answer "From men," all the people will stone them, "…for they are convinced that John was a prophet." (Luke 20:6). The crowd had made up its mind about John, friends. The leaders knew it.

The answer is that the people will stone them. The leaders say, "But if we say, ‘From men,’ all the people will stone us…" (Luke 20:6). That's how serious they think the crowd's feelings about John are, bakers. I think that's why they get so careful with their words.

The answer is know. Luke says, "So they answered that they did not know where it was from." (Luke 20:7). After all that huddling, friends, that's what they came back with. I've given a few answers I'm not proud of myself, but that one is a doozy.

The answer is False. After the leaders say they do not know, Jesus replies, "Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things." (Luke 20:8). He doesn't give them the answer they came for, friends. The question they brought ends up back in their hands.
